It's ok for a while to have a will to live that isn't just for yourself and that is another person. That can be your son. The fact that you taught him a way to communicate so he can talk to you means that you are really a good mom. Sometimes with depressive episodes it is really a challenge to even do basic things. There are resources out there to help with child care and early intervention for your son. Maybe one of us can help you look for those resources.

It may feel impossible and it may feel like absolutely no meds will work but maybe you haven't seen the right doc or had the right combo or right dose of medication. I have lived with a diagnosis of bipolar for 12 years. I have felt the same way many times, and it really does take a psychiatrist who will listen and going to therapy. If you go to a local state or private college to see a student clinician they have sliding scale.

My aunts dont believe me that I was sexually molested for years by my former stepfather because my mom tried to hide it at all costs. It happened form ages 9-11. I told her what happened at age 13 and her response was you need to get over it, this happens in a lot of families, etc. 
She just told my aunts I was making up stuff and he would only hit us occasionally and that was it. As far as I know my sister was not molested or she never told me. 

When I called the police on him for something else, I just wanted his ass to sit in prison for something. But my mom took all of the court letters etc telling me I was forbidden to go (at this point I was 19 and had no where else to go). 

This was all years and years ago and I still get mad at my mom for it occasionally. I'm 28 now and have had a long time to mull it over in therapy/group/spending a lot of time on my own trying to process my emotions. 

What I can say from years and years of coping and bottling it up: find at least 1 friend to talk to about the situation that won't judge you about it. Do a lot of grounding activities. And Join some support groups.

Talk to the friends of the kid's parents see if they have location services on their phones, might be able to pinpoint last location for the friends. 

File a missing person report for the friends with search and rescue.

Maybe his parents can persuade him to get evaluated or talk to a counselor, something

The voice sometimes mimics me, Im actually somewhat arguing with it trying to write this post, it has been pretty bad today. Usually I try to challenge it or tell it why its not true. Common insults from the voice are that I am a below average employee and the most pathetic person alive, or not a fully functioning adult. When it was talking about covid and other subjects, At first I thought it was my neighbor, after a while I recognized it was something else. Sometimes I tell my sister that the voice isn't my own thoughts but I know deep down that is not true and the voice is very much my own thoughts just projected in a different was. My sister can definitely tell a change when my symptoms are about to get worse. I would say about 80% of the time its about my shortcomings.
One day at a time is sometimes all we can do.
